title: MemUse: Moving Memory Evaluation from Direct QA to Natural Integration in Long-Term Human-AI Conversation
one_sentence: A four-month deployment shows that retrievable conversational memory is not the same as naturally integrating relevant shared history into an ongoing exchange.
problem: Does Direct QA measure whether a conversational agent uses memory in the way that matters during long-term interaction?
method: Four-month deployment with 40 users, 1,872 sessions, seven rotating memory conditions, Direct-QA comparisons, and a MemUse set of naturally cued memory moments.
findings: Existing-benchmark Direct QA varied from 19.7% to 70.1% without corresponding satisfaction differences.

For the same model and context, 78.8% of facts were answerable under Direct QA but only 7.9% were referenced naturally; Natural Integration, not Direct QA, was associated with satisfaction in the observed cue moments.
real_contribution: Separates memory availability and elicited retrieval from context-sensitive conversational use, providing a needed diagnostic layer between memory and shared meaning.
biggest_weakness: The Natural Integration–satisfaction analysis is observational and small (48 sessions/16 users), explicit cue moments are sparse, all conditions retained summary context, and the setting is text-only.
claim_boundary: Does not demonstrate mutual belief, convention, reciprocal adaptation, embodiment, or that natural memory use causes satisfaction.
why_researcher_should_care: AMSC should test retrieval, natural integration, partner-specific interpretation, and convention evidence as distinct outcomes.
evidence_notes: Open arXiv full text inspected; v1 submitted 2026-08-25 and listed as EMNLP 2026 Main.
Association is not treated as causal evidence.
